page.layout: One page of text: a running head at the top, a verse epigram in italic above, then a full-width title block, an elegy heading, and the verse of the elegy in roman below.

l.i: Quid magis est Sariis Satibus orbe frequens.
Nocte dieque rudit Monachus, cantatque Poëta
Et placet immodicè stultus Sterque sibi.
Cuique sua est Sati lasciuo Cynthia frater
Sape pius dominas quattuor snus habet.
Friget carmen aqua potori infuane poëta,
Triste canit pota frater anhelus aqua.
Accinctus cithara resonat sua carmina Sates:
Sic Monachi cingit plena lagena latus,
Hunc [illegible, ~3 letters] furor exagitat, furorque [illegible, ~3 letters] illum: I-
pse gerit thyrsos, & gerit ille cruces:
Sunt Monachis tonsa sacra corona coma.
Denique des Monacho Musas, Satiqueque cucullum

main_text.l: Nec contenta ferox ferro strauisse Quiritesᵣ Per-

page.notes: The epigram's Greek words in the fifth and sixth lines are printed in Greek letters and could not be read with certainty, so they are marked illegible. The drop-cap V of the elegy is read as V. The last line "Per-" is a hyphenated line end, kept with its hyphen. The "Quiritesᵣ" mark at the line end is a printed mark that I could not confirm.
